audit_result.proof_trace: The supply-cap check at reserve.move:89 computes `total_deposit_plus_interest.ceil() + increment - self.cash_reserve.ceil() > limit`. Because `total_deposit_plus_interest = exchange_rate * total_supply = cash + debt - cash_reserve` (reserve.move:74-84), the formula effectively evaluates `(cash + debt - cash_reserve) + increment - cash_reserve > limit`, subtracting `cash_reserve` twice. The correct check should be `total_deposit_plus_interest + increment > limit`; the extra subtraction of `cash_reserve` makes the effective cap `supply_cap + cash_reserve` rather than `supply_cap`, allowing deposits to exceed the intended limit by up to the protocol reserve balance.
audit_result.attack_scenario: As `cash_reserve` accumulates over time from interest reserve-factor accrual, flash-loan fees, and liquidation revenue, any depositor can push total user deposits above `max_deposit_amount` by up to the accumulated `cash_reserve` value; no special privilege is required beyond calling the normal `deposit` entry point.

PROP-01b-partial1-pre-003.text: Market must be active and supply + deposit <= supply_cap before mint is allowed.
PROP-01b-partial1-pre-003.assertion: mint(market, coin) requires market.active == true && market.total_supply + coin.value <= supply_cap
